title: Stream Conductor: event-first stream orchestration and idempotent retry saga for Python SDK
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: SDK users implementing streaming chat completions today must stitch low-level event frames, handle out-of-order signals (DONE/ERROR/HEARTBEAT), checkpoint partial content for resume, and implement idempotent retries across network blips. This is error-prone and leads to duplicated logic in customer code and production incidents when retries replay partial side-effects.

Proposal: Add a lightweight high-level primitive called StreamConductor in the Python SDK that is "event-first": it consumes model event frames (token/chunk/metadata/signal) and exposes a composable, single-API async iterator plus an explicit resumable checkpoint token. Core features: atomic event deduplication, idempotent retry saga semantics, explicit resume tokens, pluggable persistence hooks (in-memory / Redis / user callback), built-in telemetry hooks, and ergonomic helpers for common patterns (assemble_chat_messages, incremental_json, function-call-collector). The conductor will not replace the low-level stream API; it will sit on top and be opt-in for application developers who want safe, resilient streaming with minimal code.
acceptance_criteria: Python SDK exposes StreamConductor async context manager with __aiter__ and resume(token) semantics
Conductor emits deterministic events in original order after deduplication when retries occur
Resume token schema versioned (v1) and documented; resume(token) resumes from last acknowledged event
Built-in retry saga ensures at-most-once delivery semantics for registered side-effect callbacks
Unit + integration tests cover network interruption, replay, duplicate frames, and concurrent resume attempts
Telemetry events emitted for start/stop/retry/resume/drop with tags: model, route, customer_id (if set), duration
Backward compatibility: existing low-level streaming APIs unchanged and supported
Documentation + cookbook example added to SDK docs and one sample app in examples/stream-conductor
tasks: Design API sketch and write RFC doc in Confluence: /confluence/rd/SDK/stream-conductor-v1
Prototype conductor in experimental branch and add unit tests for dedupe and resume
Integrate persistence hook interface and implement in-memory + Redis adapters
Add telemetry hooks and wire to existing SDK telemetry layer
Add examples: chat incremental builder, incremental JSON parser, function-call collector
Code review and iterate on ergonomics with SDK PM and Design
Write docs and release notes; mark feature as experimental flag (env SDK_STREAM_CONDUCTOR=1)
Close PR and schedule canary release to internal infra customers
examples:
# usage sketch:
from redwood.sdk.streaming import StreamConductor

async with StreamConductor(client.stream_chat(...)) as conductor:
    async for evt in conductor:
        if evt.type == 'token':
            print(evt.text, end='')
        if evt.type == 'signal' and evt.name == 'DONE':
            await conductor.ack()   # advances resume cursor

# resume later:
async with StreamConductor(client.stream_chat(...)) as conductor:
    conductor.resume(token_from_previous_run)
    async for evt in conductor:
        ...
# function-call-collector example: collects a single function call and guarantees the handler runs exactly once across retries
risks_and_mitigation: Performance overhead from dedupe: add sampling-based benchmark and optimize hot-path (use deque + memcmp on small frames)
Incorrect resume tokens across model variants: version tokens and validate model metadata; fail-open with clear error messages
User misuse of side-effect callbacks leading to non-idempotent operations: provide recommended patterns and helper idempotency wrapper
Operational complexity (Redis dependency): include in-memory fallback and make persistence pluggable and optional
rollout_plan: Cut opt-in experimental flag release to SDK alpha channel (internal)
Collect telemetry for 1 week and validate resume success rates and latency impact
Invite two customer Platform teams for early access; collect feedback
Promote to stable after tests and customer feedback; include migration guide

2026-03-13 - Security (Jordan Blake): Checked threat model for resume tokens. They may leak partial user outputs; recommend encrypting tokens if used across untrusted clients. Marked security_review_required=false but added note to docs.
